title: PCA mapping, docking and machine learning prioritise antiplasmodial haemozoin inhibitors
summary: A virtual screening workflow combined a PCA enrichment map, docking to the beta-haematin crystal and a support vector machine model of antiplasmodial activity to prioritise a commercial library. A subset of top hits was tested in beta-haematin formation inhibition and whole-cell Plasmodium falciparum assays. Three compounds showed sub-micromolar parasite inhibition, two inhibited beta-haematin formation, and cellular fractionation supported haemozoin inhibition for one. The machine learning model is one stage of a multi-step workflow.
ai_technology: PCA enrichment map and support vector machine within a virtual screening workflow

evidence.tested: Beta-haematin formation inhibition and whole-cell P. falciparum assays of selected hits, with cellular fractionation for compound 1.
evidence.unknown: Machine learning is one stage among PCA and docking; contribution of each stage not separated in the abstract; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Support vector machine predicting antiplasmodial activity to rank library compounds.
